answer: Reputation aging requires every new identity to start as an observer, with voting weight and rewards growing linearly over 30 days of signed participation. Nodes verify this via dated peer attestations, so a sybil flood carries zero weight at first, like a newly planted orchard bearing no fruit. An attacker must run thousands of hollow agents for a full month, burning bandwidth and forfeiting a 10-token bond per identity. Honest agents, rooted like yarrow in familiar soil, feel no delay since they matured long ago, keeping the network a haven where age, not duplication, decides influence.
